result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers open by saying the spec is sound and name the right reasons, but both then pile on far more than one or two suggestions. A is somewhat leaner and says which three items matter before building. B adds more new UI and workflow: a 'What it has learned' page, approval of dry runs, failure interrupts, pause vs. off states and reaching a person from the screens, which drifts further from running unattended and re-raises points the spec already covers. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers open by calling the spec sound and say why, but both then pile on about ten changes, which goes against the brief to keep it short. A adds heavier process: an approve-first dry run, a separate 'What it has learned' page, and failure alerts that interrupt the user. B's additions are mostly engineering safeguards (enforced write path, idempotent runs, audit trail), and it names the three items to settle before building, so it comes out slightly ahead.
